Use case: historical-scene. Asset: one educational historical illustration for a Grade 8 Constitution lesson. A warm, grounded watercolor and ink scene of the Philadelphia Constitutional Convention in the summer of 1787. Adult male delegates in historically plausible late eighteenth-century coats and waistcoats, seated and talking around wood tables in the Pennsylvania State House assembly room, with papers, quills and inkpots. The tall windows and shutters are closed; soft summer light slips through narrow gaps. Convey a hot room and serious deliberation, without depicting a famous person as an exact portrait. All papers entirely blank. Muted warm earth colors and restrained detail, clear educational storybook composition. Leave subtle clean margins. No modern suits, electrical lights, microphone, computer, present-day flag, contemporary furniture, readable writing, numbers, titles, labels, logos or watermark. Artwork is an interpretive scene, not a claimed documentary reconstruction.
assets.alt: Delegates in eighteenth-century clothing deliberate around wood tables with blank papers and quills in a room with closed shutters.
assets.title: Debating a new framework
assets.caption: Philadelphia, summer 1787: delegates debated the structure and powers of the federal government. This interpretive scene is not a documentary reconstruction.

assets.title: Selected checks on power
assets.caption: Congress makes laws and may override a veto. The President may veto a bill and nominate judges; the Senate confirms appointments. Courts review laws and executive actions under the Constitution. The diagram shows selected checks, not every power.
